question: When sole-free recovery fails, is the chosen detection a different object, is its correctly identified box displaced by the filter, or is the new pair removed by native deduplication?
action: Read only the completed and independently audited full outputs, current raw detections, sparse labels and recorded assignments. No tracker/network/evaluator rerun, parameter tuning or update intervention.
arms: Same SUPPORT, IMAGE and FLYVIS full trajectories; add AGEonly if its separately registered full study finishes and passes its audit.

definitions.added_first_pairs: actual_first minus native_first within each variant, never by numeric ID comparison across variants.
definitions.raw_identity: Current high-confidence detections matched jointly to same-classGT at IoU>=0.5 on actually annotated frames only.
definitions.target: The emitted trajectory last-known identity if its return event exists; otherwise one consistent identity from actually labeled recent stored observations. Sources recorded; conflicts and unknowns explicit.
definitions.box_degradation: The matched raw detection has IoU>=0.5 to its known current object, but emitted filtered box has IoU<0.5 to that same object. Count separately when prior and current identity agree.
definitions.assigned_but_not_emitted: First-stage added pair has no same-variant current output. Native duplicate-removal log checked separately; absence alone is not a cause.

literature.role: OC-SORT separates a re-association from correcting the accumulated Kalman state afterwards. This motivates distinguishing two failure stages; it does not prove ORUis needed or solves identity choice here.

limitations: Historical20val and sparseGT. Local direct-edge diagnosis does not account for all later closed-loop effects. Unknowns are not negative labels. A different identity cannot be repaired merely by a better post-match Kalman update. No claim about problems2–4or a causal test of field coverage.
acceptance: All registered input hashes unchanged, native pairs retained, all direct added pairs counted once, identity and box-error populations separated. No tracker-quality acceptance inferred from this diagnostic.
